label: thm:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main}
Assume the analytic inputs of \cite{OAI26} recorded in
Section~\ref{sec:inputs}, including the family-wide
\(7/8\) zero-free half-plane.
Every finite-order Hecke \(L\)-function over
\(F=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})\) has no zeros in
\[
 \operatorname{Re} s>B_1=\frac{8748867}{10000000}
             =\frac78-\frac{1133}{10000000}.
\]
The same holds for every Dirichlet \(L\)-function,
including \(\zeta(s)\). Poles at \(s=1\) for principal
characters are allowed.
head: environment

label: lem:kappa-extension
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:kappa-extension}
The plain moment \eqref{eq:plain-moment}, with all
the preceding coefficient and uniformity conditions,
continues to hold for
\[
 13/18\le\kappa\le1.
\]
Its positive-slot hypothesis
\(\beta_*\le(1+\kappa)/2\) is unchanged.
head: environment

label: prop:low
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:low}
Assume the analytic inputs of Section~\ref{sec:inputs}.
Let \(b>0\), \(1/6\le\ell\le1/5\), and let
\(l_x=(1-b-\ell)/2\), \(l_y=(1+b-\ell)/2\),
\(h=(1+b+3\ell)/2\) satisfy
\(l_x>\ell\) and \(l_y-\ell>11b/6\).
For any fixed even system of disjoint prime windows
specified above, the arithmetic probe
\eqref{eq:physical-probe} satisfies
\[
 |\mathscr I_\eta(Z)|
       \ll_{\eta,\varepsilon} Z^{l_x/2+b/12+\varepsilon}.
\]
Define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:normalization}
 \begin{split}
 A_T(Z)&=(-1)^K Z^{-\ell/6}
      \prod_i\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_i(Z)}
                  W_i(\mathrm N p/P_i)(\mathrm N p)^{-5/6},\\
 J_\eta(Z)&=\mathscr I_\eta(Z)/(c_S A_T(Z)),
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
where \(c_S>0\) is the product of the source scalar
residues and fixed Mellin factors. Then
\(A_T(Z)\asymp(\log Z)^{-K}>0\) for all sufficiently
large real \(Z\), and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:normalized-low}
 |J_\eta(Z)|\ll_{\eta,\varepsilon}Z^{C_b(B(\ell))+\varepsilon},
 \qquad C_b(s)=s-(4+b)/6,\quad B(\ell)=11/12-\ell/4.
\end{equation}
The same probe has the absolutely convergent Poisson
representation \eqref{eq:high-identity}. Its principal
row determines a function \(H_\eta\), holomorphic on
\(\operatorname{Re} s>87/100\), with \(|H_\eta(s)-1|\le1/2\)
after a fixed initial-prime cutoff. The associated
principal Mellin term is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:principal-signal}
 f_\eta(Z)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(2)}
 Z^{C_b(s)}e^{(s-5/6)^2}
              \frac{H_\eta(s)}{L_F^S(s,\eta)}\,ds.
\end{equation}
All arithmetic data and windows are fixed before
\(Z\); the implied constants may depend on those
data and the fixed target \(\eta\).
head: environment
name: Normalized probe and low bound

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Direct estimate.}
For one rescaled subset \(J\), write
\[
 d_J=\sum_{i\in J}\ell_i=d,\quad
 X'\asymp XZ^{-d},\quad Y'\asymp YZ^{-d},\quad
 M'=1-\ell-2d,\quad \ell'=\ell-d.
\]
The source completed-row argument applies
\cite[Lemma~14.3]{OAI26} at the actual row and dual
scales. Before its special substitution
\(\ell=1/6\), its two upper branches are
\[
 M'-O/2-\Delta_H+o(1),\qquad
 M'+\frac{1+3\ell'-2M'-2\Delta_H}{4}+o(1).
\]
Here \(O\ge-o(1)\) is the powerful-row length,
and \(\Delta_H\ge-o(1)\) is the actual row deficit.
The fixed row parts have already been counted.
The structural relation used in the dual-length
bound is still
\[
 M'+\ell'-1=-3d.
\]
Thus the same argument gives the completed-row
norm
\[
 \sum_m|B_m^J|^2
 \ll Z^{M'+L_\ell(d)+\varepsilon},\qquad
 L_\ell(d)=\frac{(5\ell+d-1)_+}{4}.
\]
The Gaussian annular decomposition and common
Fourier separation are unchanged. Its exact
annular offsets enter the prescribed small loss.

The quantitative additive Gram bound,
\cite[Proposition 15.2]{OAI26}, is already stated
for general polynomially bounded \(Q,Y'\) with
\(P_a=Y'^2/Q\ge1\). Here \(Q\asymp X'Y'\) and
\(P_a\asymp Z^b\). It gives
\[
 \sum_m|A_m|^2\ll
 \frac Q{Y'}
 \left(1+P_a^{1/6}+\frac{P_a^2}{Y'}\right)
 Z^\varepsilon
\]
apart from its integrable polynomial height factor.
The second inequality in \eqref{eq:low-geometry}
absorbs \(P_a^2/Y'\) into \(P_a^{1/6}\),
uniformly for \(0\le d\le\ell\).
With the exact low-separation prefactor
\(Q^{-1/2}\), Cauchy--Schwarz yields the
per-tuple bound
\[
 (X')^{1/2}P_a^{1/12}
                     Z^{L_\ell(d)/2+\varepsilon}.
\]
Relative to the unrescaled estimate, the tuple
count, compensation coefficient and \(X'\)
factor contribute \(d-3d/2-d/2=-d\).
Since \(\ell\le1/5\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:low-saving}
 -d+\frac{(5\ell+d-1)_+}{8}\le-\frac{7d}{8}\le0.
\end{equation}
The marked slots are already inside \(B_m^J\);
they are not counted again.
All scales are positive powers of \(Z\) by
\eqref{eq:low-geometry}. Summing the fixed finite
collection of subsets proves the raw low bound.

\emph{Poisson representation and normalization.}

The source coefficientwise Poisson identity gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:high-identity}
 \begin{split}
 \mathscr I_\eta(Z)
 =\frac1{(2\pi i)^3}\int_{(3)}\int_{(3)}\int_{(2)}
 &\mathcal W(X,Y,Z;s,w,z)
 \sum_u^{(6)}(\mathrm N u)^{-z}\overline{\xi(u)}\\
 &\cdot
 \frac{\zeta_F^S(6z)L^S(w,\chi_\bullet(u))}
 {L^S(s,\eta\overline{\chi_\bullet(u)})}
       \mathfrak H_{\eta,u,Z}(s,w,z)\,dz\,dw\,ds,
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
where
\[
 \mathcal W=X^{1/2-z}Z^{s+z-1}Y^{w-1}
               e^{(s+z-1)^2}M_0(z)\widehat W_1(w).
\]
The notation \(M_0(z)\) here denotes the source
radial Mellin test, not an inverse polynomial.
It is holomorphic for \(\operatorname{Re} z>0\).
The identity is absolutely convergent on these
lines and concerns exactly \eqref{eq:physical-probe}.

The full correction is a finite sum of
holomorphic selected local factors and normally
convergent unselected products. It is not
defined by division by raw local factors.
Appendix~\ref{app:contours} verifies its required
regions and the changes below \(7/8\).

Only \(u=1\) has a principal numerator.
For this row put
\[
 H_\eta(s)=\mathcal H_{\eta,1}(s,1,1/6).
\]
A fixed initial-prime cutoff gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:H-contraction}
 H_\eta\text{ holomorphic on }\operatorname{Re} s>87/100,
 \qquad |H_\eta(s)-1|\le1/2.
\end{equation}
The scalar normalizer \eqref{eq:normalization}
is applied to both sides of \eqref{eq:high-identity}.
The source fixed-ray prime theorem gives
\[
 A_T(Z)\asymp(\log Z)^{-K}>0,\qquad
 A_T(Z)^{-1}\ll_\varepsilon Z^\varepsilon
\]
for sufficiently large real \(Z\).
Combining this with the raw low bound and
\eqref{eq:signal-low} proves \eqref{eq:normalized-low}.
The Gaussian makes \eqref{eq:principal-signal}
absolutely convergent on its defining line.
head: environment

label: prop:row-count
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:row-count}
Assume the inverse and plain moments and simultaneous
witnesses of Section~\ref{sec:inputs}, including their
coefficient and uniformity conditions. Let
\(13/18\le\kappa\le1\), with
\(\beta_*\le(1+\kappa)/2\) when \(\kappa<1\).
On a dyad \(\mathrm N u\asymp U=Z^d\), let \(\mathcal B\)
be a nonunit physical amplitude class above the
detector floor, with \(\delta=2a-1\), \(x=q/\delta\),
and \(\mathscr L=\ell/d>1/5\) by a fixed amount.
Then
\[
 \#\mathcal B\ll U^{R_\kappa(\delta,x)+\varepsilon}(1+T_1)^A,
 \qquad 0<\delta\le5/6,\quad0\le x\le1/2.
\]
On this rectangle the denominator in
\eqref{eq:row-functions} is positive, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:coarse-count}
 \frac16\le R_\kappa\le1-\frac{2\delta}{3}\le1.
\end{equation}
For prescribed bounded length ranges and a requested
loss, the slot mesh is fixed before the slot count.
For each fixed slot system and arithmetic datum,
the seminorm and polynomial height orders are finite.
head: environment
name: Detected row count

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Prime selection.}
For \(0\le z_p\le\mathscr L\), a subcollection
of whole positive-amplitude slots can be chosen
with total length at most \(z_p\) and
\[
 |Q_{\rm sel}|^2\ge U^{2qz_p-\varepsilon}.
\]
The selection is fixed within the amplitude bin,
and its loss is controlled by the common slot mesh.
To see this, order the slots by decreasing \(g_i\).
A fractional initial segment of length \(z_p\)
has average amplitude at least the full weighted
mean \(q\). Discard its last fractional slot.
The lost gain is at most \((\delta/2)\) times
the largest relative slot length.
If the positive-amplitude slots are exhausted,
their full gain is \(q\mathscr L\ge qz_p\).
Taking the mesh sufficiently small proves the
claim, including the empty selection.

Relative to a witness character
\(\psi=\nu\overline{\chi_\bullet(u)}\), the
coefficient of a physical prime is
\[
 \overline{\nu(p)}1_{p\in1_T}
  =\frac1{|T|}\sum_{\theta\in\widehat T}
                         (\overline\nu\theta)(p).
\]
This is an allowed fixed combination from \(\Theta\).
When the positive orientation is needed in the
plain moment, conjugate the entire product,
including the profiles and all selected slots.
All absolute values, masks and underlying
supports are unchanged.

\emph{Combining the witnesses.}
Fix a detector parameter \(t\in[1,3/2]\) and
subdivide by the simultaneous witnesses in
\eqref{eq:witnesses}.

\emph{Short witnesses.}
For \(r<1\), the inverse capacity is
\(z_M=(1-r)/2\); for \(m<1/2\), the plain
capacity is \(z_P=(1-2m)/(6\kappa)\).
The selected moments give the respective exponents
\[
 \begin{split}
 A_I(r)&=1-\delta\{x+(1-x)r\},\\
 A_P(m)&=1-\delta\{cx+(2-2cx)m\}.
 \end{split}
\]
Use \(m\ge t-r-o(1)\). The two expressions cross at
\[
 r_*(t)=
 \frac{(2-2cx)t+(c-1)x}{D_\kappa(x)}.
\]
For \(c\le6/13\), direct multiplication by the
positive denominator gives
\[
 3/5\le r_*(t)\le1,\qquad
 1/3\le t-r_*(t)\le1/2.
\]
Use the inverse bound for \(r\ge r_*(t)\)
and the plain bound for \(r\le r_*(t)\).
Their common value is
\[
 R_{\rm sh}(t)=1-\delta+
       \frac{\delta P_\kappa(x)}{D_\kappa(x)}
                                      (3/2-t).
\]
This choice also verifies admissibility.
The inverse selection has length at most \(1/5\).
After decreasing it by \(\nu_0>0\), its first
strict margin is \(2\nu_0\), and its second is
\[
 3-2r-8z_M=2r-1+8\nu_0\ge1/5.
\]
The selected plain length is at most
\(1/(18\kappa)\le1/13\).
Near zero capacity use the appropriate unmarked
estimate; the resulting loss is arbitrarily small.

\emph{Long witnesses and the choice of detector.}
If \(r\ge1\), \eqref{eq:long-inverse} and \(r\le t+o(1)\)
give the exponent
\[
 R_{\rm long}(t)=1-\delta+(\alpha-\delta)(t-1).
\]
If \(m\ge1/2\), the zero-slot plain moment gives
\(1-\delta+o(1)\).
Balancing the remaining two branches at
\[
 t_*=1+
 \frac{\delta P_\kappa(x)}{2\mathcal J_\kappa(\delta,x)}
\]
gives \eqref{eq:row-functions}.
At \(\delta=\alpha\), use the unmarked endpoint
\(t=3/2\); vanishing-capacity neighborhoods are
handled as above. The finite presentation choices,
dyadic subdivisions and source Sobolev bounds
give the stated uniform loss.

\emph{Denominator and coarse bounds.}
Both \(D_\kappa\) and \(P_\kappa\) are positive
on the stated rectangle, so \(\mathcal J_\kappa>0\).
The lower bound follows from \(R_\kappa\ge1-\delta\).
The identity
\[
 2D_\kappa-3P_\kappa=2x(2+c-3cx)\ge0
\]
gives \(P_\kappa/D_\kappa\le2/3\).
Hence
\(R_\kappa\le1-\delta+\delta P_\kappa/(2D_\kappa)
\le1-2\delta/3\).
head: environment

label: prop:numerator
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:numerator}
Let \(13/18\le\kappa\le1\), and assume the plain
moment \eqref{eq:plain-moment} with its stated
coefficient and uniformity conditions. When
\(\kappa<1\), assume \(\beta_*\le(1+\kappa)/2\).
Let \(\mathcal B\) be a class of nonunit physical
rows \(\mathrm N u\asymp U\), with fixed amplitude bins
as in \eqref{eq:amplitude}, total available prime
length \(\mathscr L\), and
\[
 \#\mathcal B\ll U^{R+\varepsilon}(1+H)^A,
\]
where \(1\le H\le U^{1/100}\) bounds the numerator
and physical prime-polynomial heights, and
\(0\le q\le5/12\). Choose either
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(\vartheta=qv\), where
      \(0\le v\le\min\{\mathscr L,1/(6\kappa)\}\); or
\item \(\vartheta=q/(6\kappa)\), provided
\begin{equation}\label{eq:short-gate}
 R\le(6\kappa-2q)\mathscr L.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
Then, uniformly for \(|t|\le H\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:numerator-moment}
 \sum_{u\in\mathcal B}
 |L(1/2+\vartheta+it,\overline{\psi_u^*})|
 \ll U^{(3R+1)/4-\vartheta/2+\varepsilon}(1+H)^{A'}.
\end{equation}
Here \(\psi_u^*\) induces the physical numerator.
For prescribed bounded length ranges and a requested
loss, the prime-slot mesh can be fixed before the
slot count. Once that count and the arithmetic data
are fixed, the estimate uses finitely many smooth
seminorms and a fixed polynomial height order.
It includes the primitive conductor profiles and
the restoration of the fixed excluded Euler factors.
head: environment
name: Amplified numerator average

label: eq:block-first-moment
title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Supply-limited choice.}
Consider a centrally normalized plain block
\(S_m\) of length \(D=U^m\), with the same
character orientation as the physical primes.
For \(0\le m\le1/2\), request
\[
 z_p=v(1-2m).
\]
It fits both the supply and the moment:
\[
 z_p\le\mathscr L,\qquad 2m+6\kappa z_p\le1.
\]
The nonunit row induces outside \(\Theta\).
Apply \eqref{eq:plain-moment} with two copies
of \(S_m\). To select primes, order the slots by
decreasing positive amplitude and take an initial segment
of total length at most \(z_p\). Fractional selection
would give gain at least \(qz_p\); discarding the
last fractional slot loses only the prescribed mesh
error. If the positive-amplitude slots are exhausted,
their total gain is \(q\mathscr L\ge qz_p\).
Thus \(|Q_{\rm sel}|^2\ge U^{2qz_p-\varepsilon}\).
Then
\[
 \sum_{u\in\mathcal B}|S_m(u)|^4
 \ll U^{1-2qz_p+\varepsilon}(1+H)^{A_1},
\]
so H\"older gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:block-first-moment}
 \sum_{u\in\mathcal B}|S_m(u)|
 \ll U^{(3R+1)/4-qz_p/2+\varepsilon}(1+H)^{A_2}.
\end{equation}
For \(m\ge1/2\) in a fixed bounded range,
the zero-slot moment gives the same estimate
with \(z_p=0\).

The approximate functional equation in
Appendix~\ref{app:afe} expresses the numerator
as sums of such blocks. On each dyad its
main coefficient is \(D^{-\vartheta}\).
The dual coefficient can be written
\[
 \mathcal Q_u^{-\vartheta}D^\vartheta
 =D^{-\vartheta}(D/\sqrt{\mathcal Q_u})^{2\vartheta}.
\]
The last factor belongs to a uniformly controlled
profile. The fixed-prime restorations, whole-factor
conjugations, and rowwise conductor parameters
are justified in that appendix without changing
the permitted coefficient class.
For \(m\le1/2\), \eqref{eq:numerator-balance} gives
the exponent \(-\vartheta/2\).
For \(m\ge1/2\),
\(-\vartheta m\le-\vartheta/2\).
Sum the retained dyads and absorb their logarithmic
number and the arbitrarily small rounding losses.

\emph{Full-capacity choice.}
Only the case \(\mathscr L<1/(6\kappa)\) needs
attention. The moment capacity exceeds the available
prime length only for the shortest blocks. We split
at the length where the two quantities coincide and
use absolute counting below that threshold. Put
\[
 m_0=1/2-3\kappa\mathscr L,\qquad
 \mathcal K(R)=(3R+1)/4.
\]
For \(m_0\le m\le1/2\), the full capacity
\(z_p=(1-2m)/(6\kappa)\) fits the available
prime length, and the preceding proof applies.
For \(0\le m\le m_0\), absolute ideal counting
gives \(|S_m|\ll U^{m/2+\varepsilon}(1+H)^C\).
After the dyadic coefficient, the first-moment
exponent is \(R+(1/2-\vartheta)m\).
Since \(\vartheta<1/2\), it is bounded at \(m_0\);
the exact difference is
\[
 R+(1/2-\vartheta)m_0
        -\{\mathcal K(R)-\vartheta/2\}
   =\frac{R-(6\kappa-2q)\mathscr L}{4}\le0.
\]
The dual profiles satisfy the same absolute bound.
All longer blocks were already covered.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The same prime amplitudes can be used in both the
row count and the numerator moment. They are lower
bounds that hold on every row of the chosen class;
applying two estimates to that class does not insert
two additional prime products into the probe.
head: environment

label: prop:high
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:high}
Assume the analytic inputs of Section~\ref{sec:inputs}.
Let \((b,\ell,\kappa;g,\zeta,g_*)\) be admissible,
and suppose \(\beta_*\le(1+\kappa)/2\).
If \(\Delta=\beta_*-B(\ell)>0\), there exist a fixed
even prime-slot system and \(\rho>0\), common to all
targets, such that the probe and principal term of
Proposition~\ref{prop:low} satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:high-remainder}
 |J_\eta(Z)-f_\eta(Z)|
       \ll_\eta Z^{C_b(\beta_*)-\rho}
\end{equation}
for every fixed finite-order target \(\eta\) and all
sufficiently large real \(Z\). Constants and thresholds
may depend on \(\eta\), but \(\rho\) does not.
The same slot system retains the low bound of
Proposition~\ref{prop:low}; it is fixed before \(Z\).
head: environment
name: Uniform high-side remainder

label: lem:raised-errors
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:raised-errors}
For every subset \(I\) of error slots, on
\eqref{eq:raised-lines},
\[
 \left|L^S(w,\chi_\bullet(u))
                 \prod_{i\in I}\mathcal D_i(u)\right|
 \ll U^{\vartheta+\varepsilon}(1+T_1)^C
 |L(1-w,\overline{\psi_u^*})|
                 \prod_{i\in I}P_i^{z_0-1/2+\varepsilon}.
\]
All conductor-deficit factors are used simultaneously.
head: environment

label: lem:frequency-monotonicity
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:frequency-monotonicity}
For every admissible parameter tuple,
with \(\delta,x\) fixed, \(\mathcal E\) is continuous
and increasing in \(d\), with one-sided slopes
between \(7/200\) and \(2\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:row-count},
\(\mathcal K-z_0\ge7/200\).
Where \(\vartheta=q/(6\kappa)\), the derivative is
\[
 \mathcal K-z_0+\frac{q}{12\kappa}.
\]
Where \(\vartheta=q\ell/d\), it is
\[
 \mathcal K-z_0+\frac{q\ell l_y}{d^2}.
\]
The two choices of \(\vartheta\) coincide at
\(d=6\kappa\ell\), so \(\mathcal E\) is continuous
there; its one-sided derivatives need not agree.
The second regime has \(d\ge6\kappa\ell>3/4\)
by admissibility.
Using \(R_\kappa\le1\), \(q\le5/12\),
\(\ell\le1/5\), and \(l_y<1/2\) bounds both
derivatives above by \(2\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The licensing hypothesis and Lemma~\ref{lem:kappa-extension}
make the plain moment available. Propositions~\ref{prop:row-count}
and \ref{prop:numerator} therefore apply with the
amplitude-dependent contours just established.

For intermediate rows with \(\delta\ge1/8\),
admissibility and Lemma~\ref{lem:frequency-monotonicity}
give \(\mathcal E\le-g+2\zeta<-g_*\).
For \(0<\delta<1/8\), the coarse bound in
Proposition~\ref{prop:row-count} gives
\(E_{\rm small}\le C_0+A_{\rm sm}\delta\).
The first inequality of \eqref{eq:admissible-ranges}
and the extension cost \(2\zeta<1/1000\) leave
a saving greater than \(g_*\).
At the detector floor the original pointwise contour
has endpoint \(C_0+(1/2+3\ell/2)/50\) and slope
less than \(2\), so the second inequality does the same.

For rows below \(Z^{d_{\min}}\), including the
nonprincipal unit rows, the absolute numerator bound
and full correction give exponent at most
\(C_b(\beta_*)+h(z_0-1/6)-l_y/2+2d_{\min}\).
The last inequality of \eqref{eq:admissible-ranges}
gives a saving of \(1/20\). Above \(Z^{h+\zeta}\),
the absolute \(z\)-line can be chosen sufficiently
far right to give any prescribed saving. The
underlying small-row and distant-row estimates are
recorded in Appendix~\ref{app:ranges}.

For the principal row, Lemma~\ref{lem:principal-remainder}
gives the three positive margins \(l_y/20\),
\(h/600\), and \(\mu\), where
\(0<\mu<(87/100)\min_i\ell_i\).
These complete the estimates for every term of the
Poisson representation in Proposition~\ref{prop:low}.

Choose the moment losses and common slot mesh first,
then a fixed even slot system fine enough for that
mesh. Set
\[
 \mu=\frac{87}{200}\min_i\ell_i,\qquad
 \gamma=\frac1{100}
       \min\{\Delta,g_*,l_y/20,h/600,\mu\}.
\]
Choose the detector width and remaining real losses
within these margins. For each target, fix the
required seminorm and height orders before choosing
the height exponent \(\tau>0\) small enough to absorb
their polynomial cost. Choose the external tail order
last. Appendix~\ref{app:choices} records this order
in detail. It yields \eqref{eq:high-remainder} with
\(\rho=2\gamma>0\), common to all targets.
The low bound holds for every fixed slot system,
so it holds for this same choice.

label: prop:parameters
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Parameter certificate

title: Proof
body_md:
The balanced lengths are
\[
 l_{x,0}=\frac{44783}{120000},\qquad
 l_{y,0}=\frac{55163}{120000},\qquad
 h_0=\frac{31757}{40000},
\]
and
\[
 l_{x,1}=\frac{11195177}{30000000},\qquad
 l_{y,1}=\frac{13791227}{30000000},\qquad
 h_1=\frac{7939473}{10000000}.
\]
Substitution gives the stated boundaries and
licensing identities, as well as
\[
 C_{b_1}(B_1)=\frac{2906963}{15000000}.
\]
The only inequalities over a continuous parameter
rectangle are the endpoint bounds. Clearing their
positive denominators gives the exact identities
\eqref{eq:certificate-template}. The integer
coefficients in Appendix~\ref{app:certificates}
have \(\mathcal A_j(y)>0\) and
\(4\mathcal A_j(y)\mathcal C_j(y)-\mathcal B_j(y)^2>0\)
for \(y=1/2-x\ge0\). Completing the square proves
\[
 E_{b_j,\ell_j,\kappa_j}(\delta,x)<-g_j
 \quad(0\le\delta\le5/6,\ 0\le x\le1/2).
\]
All remaining conditions are rational comparisons.
Appendix~\ref{app:ranges} records their exact values:
the low-scale margins are positive, the prime supply
exceeds \(21/100\), and the three remaining scalar
bounds are strictly below \(-1/250\), \(-1/100\),
and \(-1/20\), respectively. In the small-\(\delta\)
bound \(A_{\rm sm}>0\), so its maximum is at
\(\delta=1/8\). Finally \(g_j-2\zeta_j>g_{*,j}\)
and both \(g_{*,j}\) and \(2\zeta_j\) lie in
\((0,1/1000)\). This checks every admissibility
condition in Section~\ref{sec:high}.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:closure}
Assume the analytic inputs of Section~\ref{sec:inputs}.

and \(\beta_*\le(1+\kappa)/2\), then

head: environment
name: Closure for a licensed parameter choice

label: eq:final-comparison
title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose \(\Delta=\beta_*-B(\ell)>0\).
Proposition~\ref{prop:high} supplies one fixed
slot system and a saving \(\rho>0\) common to all
targets. For the same probe, Proposition~\ref{prop:low}
with loss \(\Delta/4\) gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:final-comparison}
 |J_\eta(Z)|\ll_\eta Z^{C_b(B(\ell))+\Delta/4},\qquad
 |J_\eta(Z)-f_\eta(Z)|\ll_\eta Z^{C_b(\beta_*)-\rho}.
\end{equation}
Since \(C_b\) has slope one, it follows that
\[
 |f_\eta(Z)|\ll_\eta Z^{C_b(\beta_*)-\epsilon_*},
 \qquad \epsilon_*=
       \min\{3\Delta/4,\rho,\Delta/2\}>0.
\]
In particular \(\epsilon_*<\Delta\), so
\(\beta_*-\epsilon_*>B(\ell)>87/100\).

The integral defining \(f_\eta\) in
Proposition~\ref{prop:low} can be moved from \(s=2\)
to any larger fixed real part. Absolute convergence
of the reciprocal and Gaussian decay then give
arbitrarily rapid power decay as \(Z\downarrow0\).
Consequently
\[
 \int_0^\infty f_\eta(Z)Z^{-C_b(s)}\,\frac{dZ}{Z}
\]
is holomorphic on \(\operatorname{Re} s>\beta_*-\epsilon_*\).
Fourier inversion on \(\operatorname{Re} s=2\) identifies this
transform with
\[
 e^{(s-5/6)^2}\frac{H_\eta(s)}{L_F^S(s,\eta)}.
\]
The identity theorem extends the identity, and
\(|H_\eta-1|\le1/2\) from Proposition~\ref{prop:low}
permits division by \(H_\eta\) throughout the region.
Thus every reciprocal \(1/L_F^S(s,\eta)\) extends
holomorphically to \(\operatorname{Re} s>\beta_*-\epsilon_*\).
The displacement \(\epsilon_*\) is common to all
targets. By the definition of \(\beta_*\), some
target has a zero to the right of that line, where
its reciprocal has a pole. This is the contradiction.

title: Proof
body_md:
Proposition~\ref{prop:parameters} supplies the two
admissible choices and their licensing identities.
The assumed \(7/8\) half-plane licenses the first
choice, so Lemma~\ref{lem:closure} gives
\(\beta_*\le B_0\). This licenses the second choice;
a second application of the same lemma gives
\(\beta_*\leB_1\).
Deleting or restoring the finitely many Euler
factors of an induced character changes no zero
in this half-plane.
The norm-pullback transfer
\cite[Proposition 11.3]{OAI26}, including the
principal case at \(s=1\), gives the Dirichlet
statement.

label: cor:mobius
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:mobius}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:main},
let \(\eta\) be a fixed finite-order Hecke character
over \(F\), and let \(W\) be smooth and compactly
supported in \((0,\infty)\). For every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \sum_{\mathfrak a}\mu(\mathfrak a)\eta(\mathfrak a)
                 W(\mathrm N\mathfrak a/X)
       \ll_{\eta,W,\varepsilon}X^{B_1+\varepsilon}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Mellin inversion expresses the sum as the
integral of
\(\widehat W(s)X^s/L_F(s,\eta)\)
on an absolute line.
Theorem~\ref{thm:main} permits its shift to
\(\operatorname{Re} s=B_1+\varepsilon\).
The logarithmic-control estimate of \cite[Section~4]{OAI26} gives
a fixed polynomial height bound for the
reciprocal on this line and on the intervening
strip. The Mellin transform of \(W\) has
arbitrary decay. Horizontal joins therefore
vanish, and the shifted integral has the
stated bound. The reciprocal of a principal
pole has a zero, not a pole.

title: Proof
body_md:
Retain the full source statement, including
its moving-support and common-puncture
conventions, as needed in its induction.
Write \(M\) for the effective width and
\(A=m_1+m_2+z\).
We check the occurrences of \(\kappa\) in
the proof of \cite[Lemma 18.1]{OAI26}.

For \(\kappa<1\), the hypothesis
\(\beta_*\le(1+\kappa)/2\) licenses the
global logarithmic-derivative bound on
\(\operatorname{Re} s=(1+\kappa)/2+e\).
Mellin inversion of the von Mangoldt sum,
removal of higher prime powers, and division
by the logarithmic weight give
\[
 |Q|^2\ll Z^{\kappa z+\varepsilon}(1+H)^A.
\]
Each resulting slot character is nonprincipal:
otherwise the inducing row character would
belong to \(\Theta\).
For \(\kappa=1\), absolute counting suffices.
The distance from the family zero boundary
is at least \(e\), uniformly on the compact
admissible parameter interval.

The affine premise and \(A\ge z\) imply
\[
 \kappa z\le M/6,\qquad z\le3M/13
       \qquad(\kappa\ge13/18).
\]
The source width-floor proof uses only the
first inequality for its extra terminal
exponent \(\rho/6\).
The old auxiliary upper bound \(2M/9\)
is replaced by \(3M/13\).

In the centered range \(A>5M/6\),
\[
 (6\kappa-1)z<M/6,\qquad
 6\kappa-1\ge10/3,\qquad z<M/20.
\]
With the same comparison length \(L=M/4\),
\[
 A-z>47M/60>2L.
\]
The reflected comparison therefore satisfies
\[
 A_{\rm comp}<23M/30+\xi,\qquad
 A_{\rm comp}+(6\kappa-1)z<14M/15+\xi.
\]
The two required comparison boundaries
retain their \(M/15\) reserve.

The finite Fourier transformations, their
coefficient identities, and exceptional-row
cancellation do not depend on \(\kappa\).
For a nonexceptional child with positive
affine defect \(F\), removing a slot of
length \(s\) decreases the affine expression
by \(6\kappa s\) and costs \(\kappa s\).
The same greedy prefix with mesh \(\eta\)
has total cost at most
\[
 \kappa\{F/(6\kappa)+\eta\}
       \le F/6+\eta.
\]
If the slots disappear, the completed
unrestricted zero-slot assertion applies.
The coefficient class is unchanged.

Finally \(0\le6\kappa-1\le5\), so the aggregate
support error is still bounded by
\[
 |\Delta M|+|\Delta A|+5|\Delta z|.
\]
These checks cover the parameter-dependent
prime estimate, terminal cap, centered
comparison, child repair and support errors.
The source strict width decrease is unchanged.

Run the same finite induction: first all
zero-slot width bands, then the positive-slot
bands. The width floor, width step, support
allowance and mesh are chosen from the
bounded real ranges and final loss before
the slot count. Their terminal and edge
reserves are exactly the ones just checked.
For each fixed slot system and arithmetic
datum, choose finite seminorm and height
orders backwards through that bounded depth.
This proves the extension, with the same
slot-count-independent mesh and the same
fixed-data uniformity.

label: lem:afe-profiles
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:afe-profiles}
For fixed nonnegative integers \(j,N\),
uniformly for \(2/5\le\sigma\le3/5\),
\[
 |(x\partial_x)^jV_w(x)|
 \ll_{j,N}
 \left(1+\frac{x}{1+|t|}\right)^{-N}.
\]
For \(\sigma=1/2+\vartheta\),
\(0\le\vartheta\le1/10\), the Euler
seminorms of
\[
 \frac{\Gamma(1-w)}{\Gamma(w)}
                   x^{2\vartheta}V_{1-w}(x)
\]
obey the same type of bound after increasing
the chosen decay order.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For \(x\ge1+|t|\), move the defining line
to a sufficiently large fixed positive
real part and apply Stirling.
For \(x\le1+|t|\), move it to \(-1/4\);
there is no gamma pole in this move, since
\(\sigma\ge2/5\), and the only residue is
the constant \(1\).
Euler derivatives insert powers of \(v\),
not powers of \(t\).
The Gaussian makes their integrals
uniformly convergent, including when
\(t+\Im v\) is bounded.
The resulting powers are those of
\(x/(1+|t|)\), which proves the first claim.
Stirling also gives
\[
 |\Gamma(1-w)/\Gamma(w)|
                \ll(1+|t|)^{-2\vartheta}.
\]
This cancels the possible factor
\((1+|t|)^{2\vartheta}\) in
\(x^{2\vartheta}V_{1-w}(x)\).
The product rule proves the derivative
statement uniformly on the indicated
compact range of \(\vartheta\).

title: Proof
body_md:
On \eqref{eq:raised-lines}, enlarge the fixed
initial-prime cutoff so that every selected
\(H_p\) is bounded away from zero.
For \(p\nmid u\), the normalized error has
the four bounds
\[
 Q^{-\operatorname{Re} s},\quad Q^{-6z_0},\quad
 Q^{4-5\operatorname{Re} s-6z_0},\quad
 Q^{1-\operatorname{Re} w-6z_0},\qquad Q=\mathrm N p.
\]
Each is at most \(Q^{-51/100}\).
Counting primes in the slot gives
\(P_i^{z_0-51/100+\varepsilon}\).

For \(p\mid u\), write \(j=v_p(u)\).
After separating \(Q^{z_0}\), the
non-strict boundary exponents are
\[
 \begin{array}{c|l}
 j&\text{exponents}\\ \hline
 1&-1-\operatorname{Re} w\\
 2&1/2-2\operatorname{Re} s\\
 3&1-2\operatorname{Re} s-\operatorname{Re} w,\quad1-3\operatorname{Re} s\\
 4&3/2-3\operatorname{Re} s-\operatorname{Re} w\\
 5&2-5\operatorname{Re} s.
 \end{array}
\]
They are strictly below \(-1/2\) because
\(\operatorname{Re} w\ge1-a\) and \(a\ge51/100\).
The geometric tails are smaller.

The remaining strict term, present for
\(j\ge2\), has exponent
\(-\operatorname{Re} w=\vartheta-1/2\).
For the complete set \(J_0\) of selected
strict ramified labels in one error tuple,
the primitive numerator conductor satisfies
\[
 \mathrm N\mathfrak f_u\ll_S \mathrm N u
       \prod_{p\in J_0}(\mathrm N p)^{-(j_p-1)}.
\]
The functional equation contributes
\((\mathrm N\mathfrak f_u)^\vartheta
 |L(1-w,\overline{\psi_u^*})|\)
and a polynomial height factor.
At each label,
\[
 -\operatorname{Re} w-(j_p-1)\vartheta
       =-1/2-(j_p-2)\vartheta\le-1/2.
\]
This is one simultaneous conductor-deficit
bound, not a repeated use of the same saving.
The labels are distinct because the physical
windows are disjoint.
Summing the divisor-many ramified labels
costs \(U^\varepsilon\).
The other deleted Euler factors are harmless,
since \(\operatorname{Re} w\ge2/5\).
The reflected \(L\)-value has been retained,
not replaced by a pointwise subpower bound.

title: Proof
body_md:
The original source interface states its
lower endpoint at least \(7/8\), so we
repeat its contour proof on \(\mathcal D_2'\).
Keep \(\operatorname{Re} s=\beta_*+e\).
Move \(w\) past its simple pole at \(1\)
to \(19/20\). In that residue move \(z\)
past \(1/6\) to \(33/200\).
The reciprocal remains to the right of
\(\beta_*\), and \(M_0(z)\) is holomorphic
for \(\operatorname{Re} z>0\).
The two scalar poles are the only ones
crossed; their product is \(c_S>0\).

The principal correction is bounded by
\(Z^{\ell\operatorname{Re} z+\varepsilon}\) with polynomial
height cost. The outside real power is
\[
 l_x/2+\operatorname{Re} s-1+h\operatorname{Re} z+l_y(\operatorname{Re} w-1).
\]
It gives the first two displayed remainders.
The error \(\mathcal R_{\eta,Z}\) gives
the third on its original global line.
Move only the main double residue right
to \(s=2\); the reciprocal is holomorphic
there and the Gaussian removes the
horizontal joins.
This is exactly \(f_\eta\), with no
additional outside Euler factor.
